arguments.value: Smart RX Systems appoints A3 Development Group as its exclusive distributor in Texas for the Smart Pharm Assist Kiosk and related products, while the company and distributor may handle exclusive distribution opportunities in other states except Florida, where Smart RX may market directly. A3 must use reasonable efforts to market the products, identify customers, enter pharmacy management services agreements, arrange customer supply and deployment of kiosks, keep customers informed, report problems and sales leads, and follow company marketing policies; Smart RX provides medication purchasing, management and training services, installation, support, maintenance, pharmacists, inventory and accounting support, and product recall handling. Payment terms include a 10% master distributor override for each customer kiosk location only if EBITDA is positive and sufficient, no payment if EBITDA is negative, payment within 90 days of the transaction, and a 40% share of net income for each customer kiosk contracted and implemented by A3, with other ownership and payment details to be set in separate series agreements; the source also says retail agreement terms will be in a separate agreement because no retail model has been developed. Smart RX keeps ownership of its products, background intellectual property, and trademarks, and A3 gets only a limited license to use the products for marketing and support; A3 may not copy, modify, or use the products beyond the agreement. The parties must keep confidential information protected and use it only for this agreement. The agreement lasts five years and then renews automatically for one-year periods unless either party gives 180 days’ notice of non-renewal or the agreement is terminated for cause; Texas law governs the agreement, and disputes are to be resolved in arbitration in Dallas, Texas, with courts in Orange County, Florida also referenced for jurisdiction and venue in the agreement.
